课程简介（中文）

《线性代数 B》是面向生命科学等对线性代数要求相对较低的非数学专业学生开设的一门重要公共数学基础课程。课程围绕线性代数核心知识层层递进展开教学，涵盖线性方程组、矩阵运算、向量空间、线性映射、特征值与特征向量、二次型等核心内容，帮助学生构建比较完整的线性代数知识体系。通过课程学习，学生将掌握线性代数理论基础，提升运用线性代数工具分析和解决实际问题的能力，为后续专业课程的学习和实际应用打下扎实的数学基础。

课程简介（英文）

Linear Algebra is a foundational public mathematics course for non-mathematics majors (life sciences, management, etc.). This course systematically covers systems of linear equations, matrix operations, vector spaces, linear mappings, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and quadratic forms. Students will build a comprehensive understanding of linear algebra and apply these tools to analyze and solve practical problems in their fields.

教学目标

The primary goal of this course is to help students gain a solid understanding of the fundamental concepts of linear algebra, thereby laying a strong foundation for learning other subjects.

教学方式

Lectures will serve as the primary method of instruction.

教学内容与进度安排

Week

Topic

Content

Readings (Strang, 6th Edition)

1

Systems of Linear Equations & Gauss Elimination

Geometric interpretation of linear equations — the row picture and the column picture. Gauss elimination; row echelon form; pivots and free variables; classification of solutions (unique, infinite, none).

Key insight: Ax = b asks for the combination of columns of A that produces b.

§1.1, §1.2, §2.1, §2.2

2

Matrix Basics

Matrix definition and notation. Matrix operations: addition, scalar multiplication, multiplication, transpose. Matrix-vector multiplication Ax as combination of columns. Special matrices: square, zero, identity, diagonal, triangular, symmetric.

§1.3, §2.4, §2.5

3

Elementary Transformations & Matrix Rank

Elementary row operations as multiplication by elimination matrices E. Row equivalence; matrix rank = number of pivots; row rank = column rank. Preview of LU factorization.

Four Fundamental Subspaces — first look: column space and row space, both of dimension r.

§2.3, §2.6, §3.1

4

Determinants — Definition, Geometry & Properties

Definition of determinants. Geometric meaning: det(A) is the volume scaling factor of x → Ax. Basic properties (multi-linearity, alternating, normalization). Computing low-order determinants; det(A) = product of pivots.

§5.1, §5.2

5

Determinant Expansion, Cramer's Rule & Inverse Matrices

Laplace (cofactor) expansion. Special determinants (Vandermonde, triangular). Cramer's rule. Inverse matrices: det(A) ≠ 0 ⇔ A invertible, computation (adjugate formula, Gauss-Jordan).

§5.2, §5.3, §2.5

6

Block Matrices & Linear Representation

Block partition; block addition, multiplication, inverses, determinants. Linear combination and span; criteria for linear representation; connection to Ax = b.

§2.4, §2.7, §1.1, §1.3

7

Linear Dependence & Rank of Vector Sets

Linear dependence and independence: definition, geometric meaning, determination via Ac = 0. Maximal linearly independent subset (basis of the span). Rank of a vector set; relationship with matrix rank.

§3.1, §3.2, §3.4

8

Vector Spaces

Vector space axioms; common vector spaces (R^n, matrix spaces, function spaces, polynomial spaces). Subspaces; basis and dimension. The Four Fundamental Subspaces: column space, nullspace, row space, left nullspace — full treatment (Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra, Part I).

§3.1–§3.5

Midterm

Midterm Examination

 

—

9

Linear Transformations & Solution Structure of Linear Systems

Linear transformations: definition, examples, matrix representation T(x) = Ax. Kernel = nullspace, image = column space. Change of basis. Homogeneous systems Ax = 0 (solution = nullspace). Non-homogeneous systems Ax = b (general solution = particular + homogeneous).

§8.1, §8.2, §2.2, §3.2, §3.3

10

Eigenvalues & Eigenvectors

Definition Ax = λx. Characteristic polynomial det(A − λI) = 0. Computation. Algebraic and geometric multiplicity. Trace and determinant from eigenvalues. Independence of eigenvectors from distinct eigenvalues.

§6.1, §6.2

11

Similarity & Diagonalization

Similar matrices: B = P⁻¹AP. Diagonalization: A = SΛS⁻¹. Condition — n independent eigenvectors ⇔ geometric = algebraic multiplicity for all λ. Powers A^k = SΛ^kS⁻¹. Fibonacci application.

§6.2, §6.3

12

Inner Product & Orthogonality

Inner product; Cauchy–Schwarz inequality; norm; angle. Orthogonality; orthogonal complement. Orthogonal/orthonormal bases. Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization. QR factorization: A = QR.

Four Fundamental Subspaces: C(A^T) ⊥ N(A), N(A^T) ⊥ C(A).

§4.1, §4.3, §4.4

13

Real Symmetric Matrices & Orthogonal Diagonalization

Real symmetric matrices: eigenvalues are real, eigenvectors orthonormal. Spectral Theorem: A = QΛQ^T. Comparison with A = SΛS⁻¹.

§6.4, §4.4

14

Quadratic Forms — Basics

Definition f(x) = x^T A x (A symmetric). Congruence transformations. Standard form (sum of squares). Methods: completing the square (Lagrange), orthogonal transformation via eigenvalues.

§6.5 + supplementary

15

Definite Quadratic Forms & Inertia Theorem

Positive/negative definite, semi-definite, indefinite. Five equivalent tests (Strang §6.5). Sylvester's criterion. Inertia theorem — the signature (p, q) is invariant. Canonical form.

§6.5 + supplementary

16

Least Squares & Data Fitting

When Ax = b has no solution: find x̂ minimizing ||b − Ax||². Geometry — project b onto C(A); error ⊥ C(A). Normal equations A^T Ax̂ = A^T b. Projection matrix P = A(A^T A)⁻¹A^T. Fitting lines/curves to data. Connection to QR and linear regression.

§4.2, §4.3

 

Weeks 17–18: Final Exam Review & Examination  |  Closed-book, cumulative

How to succeed in this course: (1) Read the assigned Strang sections before each lecture. (2) Attempt the homework problems yourself before seeking help. (3) Come to office hours — Wednesdays 1:30–3:30 PM. (4) The column picture, the Four Fundamental Subspaces, and the factorization hierarchy (LU → QR → SΛS⁻¹ → QΛQ^T) are the recurring themes — revisit them often. (5) The midterm is a checkpoint, not a finish line — the second half builds directly on the first.
